[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provides specific stretches to improve split flexibility:  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 1. Lunge stretch: Start in a lunge position, lower back knee to the ground, hold for 30 seconds.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 2. Butterfly stretch: Sit with soles of feet touching, pull heels towards body, press knees down, hold for 30 seconds.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 3. Pigeon stretch: From downward dog, bring right knee forward, straighten left leg, press hips down, hold for 30 seconds.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 4. Seated forward fold: Sit with legs straight, reach for toes, hold for 30 seconds.  
[ASSISTANT_CREATED] 5. Wall splits: Lie on back with legs up against a wall, slide legs open into a split position, hold for up to 5 minutes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant acknowledges discomfort during stretching but emphasizes the importance of flexibility in martial arts and its benefits for range of motion, balance, coordination, and injury prevention.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggests focusing on breathing and gradually leaning into stretches to manage discomfort.
